issues.problem: SMSF_NAME is not labelled as a registered, licensee or supplier name. Rule 5 maps a name to legal_name only when the data says it is the registered name. The register does list these people as approved auditors, so legal_name may be defensible under rule 4, but the mapping rests on an inference from the register's purpose rather than a stated label.
The map_values transform covers only 'Registered' and 'Suspended'. The profile may contain other status values, which would be left unmapped without comment.

The envelope sets valid_from equal to the SMSF_REG_DT registration date. Rule 10 allows valid_from only where the source states when the licence or status started. A registration date is close to that, but the envelope treats it as the start of the claim without the source saying so.

Rows are one per auditor condition, so the same auditor appears on several rows with identical entity observations. hash_row yields distinct IDs per condition row, so the same auditor's claims are duplicated. SMSF_NUM is a stable auditor identifier but is not unique per row.
Suspension dates are left unmapped to stay conservative. The status is mapped to suspended, but when the suspension began and ended is not recorded, so a suspended claim has no time bounds.
The audit firm the auditor belongs to is a real organisation that could be a related entity. It is left unmapped with a reason that is accurate but loses a possible entity link.

critique_issues.problem: SMSF_NAME is not labelled as a registered, licensee or supplier name. Rule 5 maps a name to legal_name only when the data says it is the registered name. The register does list these people as approved auditors, so legal_name may be defensible under rule 4, but the mapping rests on an inference from the register's purpose rather than a stated label.
critique_issues.suggested_fix: Confirm against the ASIC register field definitions that SMSF_NAME is the registered auditor name. If it is not clearly labelled that way, map it to entity.trading_name at confidence 0.6 or lower.

critique_issues.problem: The map_values transform covers only 'Registered' and 'Suspended'. The profile may contain other status values, which would be left unmapped without comment.
critique_issues.suggested_fix: Check the full distinct-value profile of SMSF_STATUS and add mappings for any other values that can be interpreted with confidence, leaving the rest unmapped.

critique_issues.problem: The envelope sets valid_from equal to the SMSF_REG_DT registration date. Rule 10 allows valid_from only where the source states when the licence or status started. A registration date is close to that, but the envelope treats it as the start of the claim without the source saying so.
critique_issues.suggested_fix: Either justify in the config that the registration date is the start of registration status, or leave valid_from null and keep the registration date only in entity.date_registered.

critique_issues.problem: Rows are one per auditor condition, so the same auditor appears on several rows with identical entity observations. hash_row yields distinct IDs per condition row, so the same auditor's claims are duplicated. SMSF_NUM is a stable auditor identifier but is not unique per row.
critique_issues.suggested_fix: Document that each row is a condition-level copy of the same auditor claims, or deduplicate observations per SMSF_NUM. Consider keeping SMSF_NUM as a traceable source key in the record ID.

critique_issues.problem: Suspension dates are left unmapped to stay conservative. The status is mapped to suspended, but when the suspension began and ended is not recorded, so a suspended claim has no time bounds.
critique_issues.suggested_fix: Keep the exclusion if preferred, but note that the suspended status observation has no validity window. Alternatively map the suspension dates to valid_from and valid_to on the status observation if the source states them.

critique_issues.problem: The audit firm the auditor belongs to is a real organisation that could be a related entity. It is left unmapped with a reason that is accurate but loses a possible entity link.
critique_issues.suggested_fix: Keep it unmapped for now, and consider a relationship or link mapping in a later iteration.
